nodes.title: The frequency beneath the frequency
paragraphs: You set TAVI to listen past the loudest radio message, down into the thin hiss that every transmission carries. Deep inside it is a second signal. Not a voice: the sound of footsteps crossing a metal corridor, one after another, although no microphone on Starport Nine is near a corridor.

Ren turns down the lights so you can hear without distraction. It is a ridiculous instruction—darkness should not make a radio louder—but when the room grows dim, the footsteps separate into two sets. One belongs to someone running. The other keeps pace without ever touching the floor.

TAVI points at the clock. The footsteps are recorded one minute before the first warning, in a minute that has not happened. Whoever is making them is either inside tomorrow or inside the mirror's memory of it.

choices.label: Follow the quieter footsteps
choices.detail: Listen for what the second person is carrying.
choices.outcome: You hear the chime of a cargo sensor and mark its timing.

choices.label: Ask Ren to compare the echoes
choices.detail: They know the sound of every deck's floor panels.
choices.outcome: Ren identifies the echo as Dock Seven's old service corridor.

illustration.alt: Illustration of Starport Nine's mirrored signal anomaly.

nodes.act: ACT IV / INSIDE THE ECHO · 20 OF 36
nodes.title: The dock that wasn't there
paragraphs: TAVI projects a map around the sound. It draws Dock Seven beside Dock Seven, two identical hallways sharing the same doors. On the first map the Wren arrives. On the other the ship vanishes into the ice ring.

The two maps disagree on a small detail: the station clock is mounted three meters higher in the second hallway. Ren has a theory that the mirror stores possibilities the way a camera stores photographs. “Only,” they say, “we've accidentally started walking around inside one.”

You put your finger on the false clock. The projection blinks, and a child's silhouette appears beneath it. For one terrible second you think it is Mika waiting on the wrong dock. Then the figure lifts an arm and you recognize the shape of your own jacket.

choices.label: Photograph the wrong clock
choices.detail: A small inconsistency may be the key to identifying the echo.
choices.outcome: The image becomes a reference marker in the storm map.

choices.label: Warn the crew about the doubled dock
choices.detail: A convincing illusion could fool an experienced pilot.
choices.outcome: Osei orders every crew member to use the real clock as a reference.

nodes.act: ACT IV / INSIDE THE ECHO · 21 OF 36
nodes.title: A message from a version of you
paragraphs: The silhouette makes the same motion you make, half a second before you think of moving. Its voice arrives over the dead channel: “Don't try the easy path. That's how the dock disappears.”

You ask the figure who it is. There is a pause long enough for you to hear Ren breathing, and then the answer: “Someone who already tried the bright door.” The figure steps sideways. Behind it is a much darker hallway and a faint red light that might be a way out.

TAVI is unusually quiet. Finally it says, “A mirrored signal can be useful evidence, but I recommend not trusting it with the entire future.” You have to decide which part of the echo deserves another look.

choices.label: Study the warning's coordinates
choices.detail: The numbers might reveal why the bright door is dangerous.
choices.outcome: You discover that the false dock is a reflection off the ice, not a second station.

choices.label: Follow the red light instead
choices.detail: Perhaps the echo is trying to show you its missing passenger.
choices.outcome: The red light leads you away from Mika's signal and toward a hidden cargo channel.

nodes.act: ACT IV / INSIDE THE ECHO · 22 OF 36
nodes.title: Mika on the wrong side
paragraphs: The signal opens into a brief picture of the Wren's cockpit. Mika is there, younger than the calm voice you have been hearing, and frightened enough to grip both sides of the pilot's chair.

“There are two stations,” Mika says. “One keeps asking us to come closer.” You hear a captain's voice in the background, sharp with frustration. The Wren is losing time and fuel. The crew cannot circle forever while the clocks argue.

You want to tell Mika everything at once: about the two clocks, about the version of you in the corridor, about the warning that arrives before it is sent. Instead you choose one thing they can use. A useful warning is better than a frightening explanation.
When the picture fades, your console shows an image of tomorrow's dock as though someone has saved it in a folder called BEFORE.

choices.label: Tell Mika which clock is real
choices.detail: Give them a physical landmark that can't lie.
choices.outcome: Mika turns off the automatic guidance display and focuses on the actual station.

choices.label: Send the reflection's timing
choices.detail: Help the Wren work around the false images.
choices.outcome: The ship changes speed just enough to slide past the brightest ice.

illustration.alt: Illustration of Starport Nine's mirrored signal anomaly.

nodes.act: ACT IV / INSIDE THE ECHO · 22 OF 36
nodes.title: The passenger no one listed
paragraphs: The red light takes you into a cargo frequency nobody has used for years. Instead of the Wren's cockpit, the console shows a small passenger cabin full of seedling crates. One crate sits open. Someone has drawn a little tree on the inside of its lid.

A message scrolls across the cargo sensor: THE SEEDS REMEMBER THE WAY HOME. Ren laughs nervously. “Wonderful. Our plants are giving navigation advice.” Then they see the numbers beneath the message. It is a pulse code that changes every time the ship approaches the false dock.

You recognize the rhythm from Dock Seven's bell. The cargo sensor isn't predicting tomorrow; it is reacting to the real Wren from across the time distortion. The last surviving Pel seedlings have become the most reliable beacon on board.
There is no time to explain how a tree can help steer a spaceship. You save the code and head back to the main signal.

choices.label: Use the seedling pulse as a beacon
choices.detail: The living cargo has a signature the ice cannot copy.
choices.outcome: TAVI marks the real ship with a steady green outline.

choices.label: Tell Mika to secure the crate
choices.detail: Protect the seedlings before their sensor becomes the target.
choices.outcome: The little plants are safe, and Mika now trusts your strange instructions.

illustration.alt: Illustration of Starport Nine's mirrored signal anomaly.

nodes.act: ACT IV / INSIDE THE ECHO · 23 OF 36
nodes.title: A signal that wants to be believed
paragraphs: Every screen on the console now shows the same pale outline of a ship. The image is so clean and bright that you almost trust it. Under it, the original radio message plays again, quieter than the first time: “Don't open the door.”

But the signal has changed. After the warning comes a soft thud, three rapid taps, and one slow tap. You hear the rhythm of Ren's tools, the old docking bell, and Mika's frightened count all in the same four notes. Different people, different days, one small pattern.

You realize the mirror may not be sending people backward in time at all. It may be sharing the same warning across multiple possible approaches until one of them leads home. If you choose the wrong one, tomorrow could lose the chance to warn today.
Ren rests a hand on the console. “We need a rule,” they say. “Not a beautiful picture. A rule we can tell the crew.” You agree, though you're not yet sure which rule will survive the storm.

choices.label: Write down the four-note pattern
choices.detail: Carry one reliable signal into the final decision.
choices.outcome: TAVI adds the rhythm to your evidence log.

choices.label: Give the evidence to Chief Osei
choices.detail: A shared understanding may be stronger than a private discovery.
choices.outcome: The chief asks everyone to stop using the automatic dock arrows.

nodes.act: ACT V / UNDER THE SHUTTER · 25 OF 36
nodes.title: A note beneath the door
paragraphs: The translator has been repaired or worked around, but the damaged message still haunts the docking console: OPEN HATCH, it says, when it means HOLD POSITION. While Chief Osei gathers the bridge crew, Ren points to a handwritten note tucked beneath the emergency shutter.

It is addressed to YOU, in handwriting you don't recognize. The note says the mirror can be turned manually if the main control room loses power. Beneath the instruction someone has drawn a tiny wrench with a smiley face. Ren insists that part is not theirs.

You could join the meeting and present what you've learned. But the voice from tomorrow is fading, and there might not be time for a committee to finish disagreeing. You follow Ren down a narrow service ladder into the machinery underneath Dock Seven.

choices.label: Take a repair kit with you
choices.detail: There's no point finding the mirror if you can't fix it.
choices.outcome: Ren lends you their favorite wrench and marks the manual motor access.

choices.label: Send Osei a quick summary
choices.detail: Someone on the bridge should know where you've gone.
choices.outcome: Osei promises to keep the shelters safe while you investigate.

illustration.alt: Illustration of the empty maintenance deck beneath Dock Seven.

nodes.act: ACT V / UNDER THE SHUTTER · 26 OF 36
nodes.title: The battery in the wall
paragraphs: Under the shutter, the station sounds older. You hear water in the heating pipes, the clicking of mechanical relays, and the steady groan of metal trying to hold the cold outside. Every modern display is gone. The only map is a paper diagram bolted to the wall.

Ren points out a battery sealed inside a dusty emergency cabinet. “We've been trying to get the budget to replace that since I started here.” The battery has enough charge for the mirror, or for the shelter lights, but not both.

Above you, the station's public address system repeats a calm voice telling everyone to remain in place. You recognize TAVI's voice, though it sounds unusually tired. The computer is using every spare circuit to keep people from panicking.
Ren does not say which circuit you should take. That makes this choice feel more difficult than an argument would.

choices.label: Keep the shelter circuit intact
choices.detail: Look for another, riskier source of power.
choices.outcome: A narrow service line gives you a little charge without putting anyone in the dark.

choices.label: Take the sealed battery
choices.detail: Give the mirror enough power to move, and accept the damage elsewhere.
choices.outcome: The motor warms under your hands; the corridor lights flicker behind you.

nodes.act: ACT V / UNDER THE SHUTTER · 27 OF 36
nodes.title: A station of strangers
paragraphs: At the bottom of the ladder you reach a corridor filled with people. They're not actually there: the glass storm is reflecting another possible evacuation through the wall. Some are heading to safety. Some run the other way, toward a door marked DOCK SEVEN.

A small child in the reflection points toward you. You know the child can't see you. Still, you want to wave. Ren gently pulls your hand down. “The mirror loves making us care about things we can't reach,” they say.

Two paths split around the motor assembly. One crosses the electrical floor where the station's power is stored. The other follows a ventilation shaft where you can still hear Mika's voice. Neither seems safe, and the chief cannot help from the bridge.
You realize the choice isn't only about danger. If you pick one path, there will not be time to investigate the other before the storm peaks.

choices.label: Cross the electrical floor
choices.detail: Find the motor controls before the storm consumes the power feed.
choices.outcome: The static tingles against your gloves as you find a maintenance switch.

choices.label: Follow Mika's voice through the vents
choices.detail: Understand what the Wren needs before moving heavy machinery.
choices.outcome: The voice sounds closer with every step, as if tomorrow is just behind a wall.

illustration.alt: Illustration of the empty maintenance deck beneath Dock Seven.

nodes.act: ACT V / UNDER THE SHUTTER · 28 OF 36
nodes.title: The manual crank
paragraphs: The floor grates are warm beneath your boots, and the mirror's motor hums through the metal. You find a manual crank, a heavy wheel designed for emergencies when the control room has failed.

Ren explains the tradeoff in the blunt way engineers do: turning the crank could point the mirror at the right place, but if you misread the old scale, the station will flash a rescue beacon straight into the ice ring. The motor won't stop halfway.
You take the wheel. The metal is colder than anything you've touched today. A line on the gauge moves one degree, then two, then stops. Something on the other side is pushing back.
Ren looks at the gauge, not at you. “No heroics,” they say. “We need the real ship, not a dramatic rescue story.”

choices.label: Match the old mirror scale
choices.detail: Use the mechanical markings instead of the bright computer arrows.
choices.outcome: The mirror moves into a workable angle, though the motor complains.

choices.label: Stabilize the motor first
choices.detail: Protect the crew from a sudden surge of electricity.
choices.outcome: Ren wedges the crank in place and the emergency circuit steadies.

nodes.act: ACT V / UNDER THE SHUTTER · 28 OF 36
nodes.title: The voice behind the panel
paragraphs: The narrow ventilation path smells of dust and hot metal. As you climb, Mika's voice grows so clear that you expect to find the Wren's cockpit behind the next panel.

Instead you find an empty service alcove. Through a small maintenance window the real Dock Seven lies fifty meters below, completely dark. A whisper says, “If you open the shutter, the bright dock comes in first.” It's your voice again, from a day you haven't lived.

Ren turns to you. “You can still go back to the motor,” they say, “but I don't think the person in that voice wants us to.” You kneel beside the panel and watch a faint blue pulse pass along the outer mirror. Unlike the bright false dock, it reflects only once.
The pulse gives you a way to recognize the true ship without ever touching the motor. But carrying that message to Control will take precious seconds.

choices.label: Record the blue pulse
choices.detail: Bring evidence instead of another guess.
choices.outcome: The signal's narrow frequency becomes a reliable marker for tomorrow's crew.

choices.label: Keep Ren listening while you call Osei
choices.detail: Share the warning with the people on the bridge.
choices.outcome: Osei orders the shutter sealed and asks you to return with the recording.

illustration.alt: Illustration of the empty maintenance deck beneath Dock Seven.

nodes.act: ACT V / UNDER THE SHUTTER · 29 OF 36
nodes.title: The decision nobody authorized
paragraphs: You climb back into the main corridor just as a warning chime echoes through the station. The Wren is making its final turn. Chief Osei is still speaking to the bridge crew, and their voices crowd the radio with proposals.

You are carrying something that might be crucial: a working mirror angle, a safe pulse, a little extra charge, or the memory of a voice that warned you against the easy path. None of it feels certain enough to save a ship by itself.

Ren offers to tell the chief you acted alone. “That way, if the plan goes wrong, they can be angry at me instead,” they say. You shake your head. The choice was yours. The responsibility belongs to you, too.
The hatch remains shut. Whatever else happens tonight, you are beginning to understand that being brave means listening to the consequences of your decisions, not escaping them.

choices.label: Report honestly to Osei
choices.detail: Trust the chief with every part of your plan, including the risks.
choices.outcome: Osei is stern for one breath, then thanks you for coming back.

choices.label: Keep control of the manual switch
choices.detail: The mirror may still need a quick human response.
choices.outcome: You return to Control with the override key tucked into your palm.

nodes.act: ACT VI / THE MANUAL RESCUE · 31 OF 36
nodes.title: The switch behind the wall
paragraphs: The bell has gone silent, but the wall beneath Dock Seven is still vibrating. TAVI says the outer mirror's motor can be reached through an emergency service tunnel. It was built before the automated guide lights, when people still turned the equipment by hand.

You tell Osei where you're going. The chief gives you one of those looks adults use when they want to say no but know there isn't time. “Do not open the hatch,” they say. “Whatever you see through the glass, do not let it into the station.”

Ren joins you at the tunnel entrance. They carry a heavy torch, a tool kit, and an expression of stubborn loyalty. You carry the old warning in your head. The two of you crawl past pipes that shiver with the storm.

choices.label: Check the tunnel's emergency breakers
choices.detail: You may need a safe way to stop the motor.
choices.outcome: The breakers respond, and you memorize the sequence for cutting power.

choices.label: Ask Ren to check the safety rope
choices.detail: The tunnel is narrow, but gravity has already failed once.
choices.outcome: The rope holds, and Ren has your back if the storm shifts again.

illustration.alt: Illustration of a daring rescue at the outer docking mirror.

nodes.act: ACT VI / THE MANUAL RESCUE · 32 OF 36
nodes.title: A window full of doors
paragraphs: The tunnel ends at a narrow maintenance chamber with one round window. Beyond it are not one but seven bright rectangles, each shaped like Dock Seven. Some drift together like reflections in a shop window. Others tilt sharply toward the ice.

Ren says the mirror motor can turn only ninety degrees. The storm has been showing people hundreds of imaginary directions, and the motor cannot possibly follow them all. For the first time, the impossible pictures seem less powerful than the very ordinary machine in front of you.

A handwritten warning sits above the crank: DO NOT FOLLOW THE BRIGHTEST LIGHT. YOU WILL NOT LIKE WHERE IT GOES. The handwriting is old and familiar. You remember the message under the shutter and wonder how many generations of station crews have tried to leave this exact warning.

choices.label: Set the crank to the marked safe angle
choices.detail: Use the manual gauge instead of the glimmering windows.
choices.outcome: The motor turns slowly, and the false docks begin sliding out of sight.

choices.label: Save power before turning the crank
choices.detail: A rescue attempt needs more than a beautiful signal.
choices.outcome: Ren finds a spare capacitor and connects it to the emergency line.

nodes.act: ACT VI / THE MANUAL RESCUE · 33 OF 36
nodes.title: The person in the second window
paragraphs: As the last bright rectangle fades, a person appears behind it. They're wearing a cadet's jacket exactly like yours. Their face is hidden by the glare. The figure holds a hand against the glass, and you instinctively do the same.

The other hand moves before yours. It points toward a small blue lamp above the service hatch, then toward the mirror. The message is obvious enough that you wish it were reassuring: the bright pictures are false; the little blue light is telling the truth.
Ren sees only an empty window. That makes you uncertain about what you've learned. A clue only you can see may still be real, but it isn't proof you can hand to a room full of frightened people.
A faint metallic knock echoes from your side of the glass. It has the same four-note rhythm as the original warning, only slower. Tomorrow, it seems, is beginning to run out of patience.

choices.label: Record the faint blue light
choices.detail: Bring a measurement the other crew can verify.
choices.outcome: The narrow pulse lines up with the ship's distress frequency.

choices.label: Tell Ren exactly what you saw
choices.detail: Another person deserves the truth, even when it's strange.
choices.outcome: Ren trusts you enough to turn the mirror without needing to see the figure.

illustration.alt: Illustration of a daring rescue at the outer docking mirror.

nodes.act: ACT VI / THE MANUAL RESCUE · 34 OF 36
nodes.title: An order over the open channel
paragraphs: Chief Osei calls from the bridge. The station is ready to abandon the rescue if the storm grows any brighter. You can hear worry behind the chief's careful words. The shelters are full. Every ordinary rule says to keep the shutters sealed until daylight.

Mika's voice arrives through a second speaker. “We have enough fuel for one more pass,” they say. “If the dock isn't there, we go back.” The Wren's captain agrees, though you can hear that they do not like giving an unknown cadet so much responsibility.

You look at the crank in your hands. Turning it could point a real signal across the ice, or it could break the outer mirror at exactly the wrong moment. In the old flight books, every rescue decision is written as a simple instruction. Here, with the metal cold and the radio full of people waiting, it feels anything but simple.

choices.label: Ask the captain for one careful pass
choices.detail: The crew should know what you can promise—and what you cannot.
choices.outcome: Mika repeats the fuel margin and confirms they can abort safely.

choices.label: Adjust the mirror by hand
choices.detail: A slow, measurable signal may beat the bright false images.
choices.outcome: The motor turns to the blue mark. Your glove is shaking when you let go.

nodes.act: ACT VI / THE MANUAL RESCUE · 35 OF 36
nodes.title: A rescue that still has a price
paragraphs: The mirror hums, its blue pulse small against the vast silver storm. For a second you see the Wren move through a clean gap in the ice. Then a shard passes between the ship and station and the signal splits into two.
You can keep pushing the motor toward the ship, but doing so may overload the docking clamps. Or you can cut power and send the Wren around the long route, leaving the impossible warning unexplained.

Ren presses a hand against the wall to feel the motor's vibration. “We can get them home,” they say. “But I can't promise the station will look the same afterward.” That is the most helpful kind of honesty: it gives you a real choice instead of a comforting lie.
You climb out of the tunnel and return to Control. Osei has kept the door sealed just as promised. The final command is still waiting for you.

choices.label: Keep the manual override ready
choices.detail: You'll accept repairs if they mean bringing people home.
choices.outcome: The crank locks into a stable rescue angle, and the crew braces for a hard landing.

choices.label: Prepare the return-route signal
choices.detail: A mission can fail without losing the people on it.
choices.outcome: The crew draws up an abort route for the Wren and protects the shelters.
